problems: The mechanic’s cap reads as a large rectangular slab in both variants, not a low, sloping flat cap. The empty tray provides little occupational identification.
The clerk’s skirt reads as two trouser-like box shells, particularly on the taller character. The central split and straight panel edges undermine the bustle-dress silhouette.
The messenger and railway baron have broad, rigid shoulder blocks that read more like shoulder armour than draped pelerines.
The railway baron reads as a well-dressed local traveller. The tiny luggage markings cannot establish distant origin or railway affiliation at stream scale.
Much of the secondary identification depends on tiny buttons, chains and labels; these should support, not substitute for, larger silhouette and colour cues.

OVERALL: The Alderman is the only kit that passes on its own. The top hat and the linked brass chain with its medallion read instantly. Two of the four everyday kits still lose their period silhouette, and the Workshop Mechanic's cap has now failed the same way two rounds running.

Workshop Mechanic: the 'sloping flat cap' still reads as a tall mustard brick or fez on both wearers. The crown box is 0.37 x 0.36 in plan and coloured with the bright 'hat' role. From the raised camera its top face shows as a second tall rectangle the same colour, so a 0.07 m slab looks about 0.25 m tall. The 0.035 'hat:dark' peak is lost under it.

Workshop Mechanic: from the waist down this is the base figure: straight trousers plus boots. On wearer 1 the base trousers are blue, so the legs read as modern jeans with work boots. Nothing below the waistcoat says 1880s.
Workshop Mechanic: the gold 'watch chain' (hips box at [-0.12,0.25,0.194], 0.16 long, rot z -0.2) floats on the waistcoat as a loose stick. It doesn't connect to a button or pocket.

Workshop Mechanic and Market Provisioner both carry an open brown and brass box at hip height (carpenter's tray, produce hamper). At stream scale these two props are the same shape, which blurs two of the four kits.

Municipal Clerk: the 'open-panel skirt' renders as two wide trouser legs with a hard vertical split down the centre front. On the navy wearer it reads as modern wide-leg culottes or palazzo trousers, not the long practical skirt rules.people asks for. The bustle sphere is only at the back and does not show in a front or 40-degree view.

Municipal Clerk: the ledger is a dark-teal slab (#263f40) hanging off the left hand, angled at rot [-0.2,-0.25,0.08]. It reads as a black handbag or tablet. The cream page block (#d3c7aa) sits 0.006 inside the cover and never shows, and the dark cover vanishes against the dark skirt.
Municipal Clerk: there is no headgear, only a small bun. From above, the figure's only period cue is the puffed sleeves. The silhouette top is the same flat-headed box as the base figure.

Market Provisioner: the apron is split into one cream panel per leg (legL/legR boxes 0.22 wide) with a gap in the centre. Each panel carries a grey pocket square, so it reads as cream shorts or dungarees with blue or ochre shins below, not a canvas market apron. The broad hat and bib work.

Telegraph Messenger: the 'pelerine' is two separate rotated boxes on the arm bones (0.21 x 0.22 x 0.34, rot z ±0.12). They render as square football or armour shoulder pads with a visible gap at the neck. Because they are on the arms, they swing apart when the figure walks. The rear 'cape' panel does not show from the front.

Railway Baron (leader): the Inverness capelet is built exactly the same way as the Messenger's pelerine, as two terracotta shoulder blocks on the arm bones, so it reads as orange shoulder armour. It also gives the leader the same shoulder silhouette as an everyday kit, which weakens 'clearly from far away'.

Railway Baron (leader): he holds a cream rolled document in his right hand, like the Alderman's charter, so the head and the leader share a prop silhouette. The 'foreign' cues are a 0.15 m sticker and a 0.21 m gold watch-chain bar, both invisible at stream scale. From far off he reads as a local man in a beige suit with a suitcase, not a visiting railway magnate.

Alderman (head): the cream lapel boxes and the grey shirt-front panel read as a pale bib or napkin under the chin, which competes with the chain. The coat is one flat colour, so the waistcoat the rules ask for is not visible.
fix:
Workshop Mechanic: Rebuild the cap with a shallow, tapered crown flowing into a short peak; eliminate the large square outline visible in this render and seat it closely against the head. Add one chunky hammer or spanner projecting above the tray rim, with the handle clearly held. Municipal Clerk: Replace the parallel box-shell appearance with slightly flared, layered skirt panels. Stagger front and rear edges so the centre reads as a fabric opening rather than a trouser division; retain separate leg attachment and test clearance through walking poses. Preserve the puff sleeves, bustle, bun and ledger. Market Provisioner: Keep the broad hat, cream bib and colourful hamper; these already distinguish the role. Refine the lower apron panels into thinner, slightly overlapping-looking canvas flaps at rest, without joining the legs, and preserve a visible hand-to-handle grip. Telegraph Messenger: Keep the peaked cap, diagonal satchel and contrasting stockings. Thin the shoulder pieces, slope their outer edges downward and align them visually with the rear cape so they read as cloth rather than rigid pads. Alderman: Retain the tall top hat, dark coat and large medallion. Seat the collar links close to the garment and continue the gold treatment over the shoulders for stronger overhead recognition; no major redesign needed. Railway Baron: Preserve the cream coat and bowler contrast with the Alderman, but soften the shoulder slabs into a draped, articulated cape. Introduce a bold invented distant-railway identity: a broad contrasting cape border and matching large locomotive or winged-wheel crest on the luggage. Move the luggage marking onto its outward-facing side and enlarge it substantially; keep all handles and carried documents visibly seated in the hands. / WORKSHOP MECHANIC
- Cap: drop the 0.37 x 0.36 box crown. Use one flattened sphere on the head at [0,0.33,0.04], size [0.34,0.10,0.36], rot [0.25,0,0], so the front dips over the brow. Add a peak box at [0,0.295,0.2], size [0.28,0.03,0.12], rot [0.18,0,0]. Colour both fixed #42494c (tweed), or the peak #263f40, NOT the 'hat' role, so it never renders mustard. Keep "hair" unhidden so hair shows at the sides under the cap.
- Trousers: replace the jeans look. Add per-leg work-trouser shells in fixed corduroy #8b6245 at [0,-0.2,0], size [0.2,0.4,0.22]. Add tall lace-up boots per leg at [0,-0.62,0.03], size [0.22,0.36,0.25] in #263f40, with a 0.04 cuff band in #42494c at y -0.45.
- Braces: two shirt:dark straps, 0.04 wide, from the waistband to the shoulder over the waistcoat edges.
- Watch chain: replace the floating bar with a short drooping 3-link chain in #b8914e, from a waistcoat button at x 0.05 to the pocket at x -0.12. Each link is 0.035 wide, placed on the waistcoat surface at z 0.19.
- Prop: replace the open tray with a CLOSED tall tool bag. armR box at [0,-0.62,0.06], size [0.14,0.22,0.28], in #263f40, with a #8b6245 leather top flap. Add a big spanner (#a7a397 box 0.04 x 0.30) sticking up out of it, so it no longer matches the hamper.

MUNICIPAL CLERK
- Skirt: make the top a hips-bone bell, box [0.56,0.34,0.38] at [0,-0.08,0] in pants:dark, wider than the hips so it hides the split.
- Lower skirt: per-leg panels widened to 0.26, shifted 0.03 toward the centre line (x -0.03 on legL, +0.03 on legR) so they overlap at the front and the centre gap disappears. Taper them to a flared hem with a 0.06 accent:dark hem band at y -0.72.
- Bustle: move the bustle up and make it bigger so it shows in the 3/4 view: sphere [0.44,0.3,0.26] at [0,-0.02,-0.2].
- Hat: add a small tilted boater or riding hat. Cylinder brim [0.34,0.03,0.30] at [0,0.36,0.03] plus crown cylinder [0.22,0.09,0.2] in 'hat', with a 0.03 'accent' ribbon. Keep the bun visible behind it.
- Ledger: make it a large cream book, box [0.06,0.30,0.24] in #d3c7aa, with dark #263f40 covers 0.012 thick on both sides. Clamp it under the left arm against the hip (armL [0.0,-0.3,0.05]), flat face to the camera, so the cream page block shows.

MARKET PROVISIONER
- Apron: replace the two per-leg leg panels with one hips-bone apron skirt, box [0.42,0.48,0.03] at [0,-0.2,0.17] in #d3c7aa. Hang it from the waist so it stands clear of the swinging thighs; the 0.03 thickness and 0.03 offset keep it from looking like shorts.
- Pockets: one wide pocket band across the apron (#a7a397, [0.3,0.1,0.02]) instead of two leg squares.
- Neckerchief: add a 0.05 rolled neckerchief in 'accent' at the collar.
- Hamper: keep it, but make it a round-handled wicker basket (cylinder body #b8914e plus an arched handle) so it differs from any box.

TELEGRAPH MESSENGER
- Pelerine: delete the two arm-bone shoulder boxes. Build it on the hips bone as one continuous capelet: box [0.70,0.16,0.38] at [0,0.50,0] in shirt:dark, plus a lower tier [0.64,0.08,0.36] at [0,0.42,0] so it steps down like a cape.
- Back: keep the cape-bone back panel, but bring its top to the shoulders.
- Fit: keep the capelet within 0.06 of the shoulder line so swinging sleeves pass under it.
- Keep the kepi, the knickerbockers with grey stockings, the brass buttons and the satchel; those work.

RAILWAY BARON (LEADER)
- Capelet: rebuild the Inverness cape the same way as the Messenger's pelerine, on the hips bone. Make it longer than the Messenger's, to the elbow: box [0.74,0.36,0.40] at [0,0.40,-0.01] in #c27f59 (tartan-brown), with a cream #d3c7aa collar band.
- Back: lengthen the cape-bone panel to y -0.6.
- Props: move the rolled concession map from his hand into a long leather map tube (#8b6245 cylinder 0.07 x 0.55) slung diagonally across his back on the hips bone. That frees the right hand for a tall walking cane with a brass knob (#b8914e).
- 'From far away': put large foreign trunk labels on the portmanteau, two or three 0.10 x 0.08 patches in #83b6bd, #d9534f and #f2cf83. Pin a broad railway-company sash or armband in #d9534f (red) with a brass crest disc 0.10 across on the chest.
- Bowler: add #263f40 travel goggles on the bowler band, or a #a7a397 dust veil, so the head says 'arrived by rail'.

ALDERMAN (HEAD)
- Keep the top hat, the chain and the charter.
- Lapels and shirt: make the lapels dark silk #1f2426. Shrink the shirt front to a 0.12-wide white collar and stock at the throat.
- Waistcoat: add a visible waistcoat panel in a rich fixed colour (#a26048 or #596f52), so the coat is not a flat dark-teal block and the chain sits on contrast.
- Cuffs: optionally add brass cuff bands on both sleeves.
